title: A Lie-Jordan Geometric Formulation of Lindblad Dynamics
authors: Leonel Bixano, Victor Alberto Cruz-Barriguete, Guillermo López-Alvarez, V. G. Ibarra-Sierra, José Luis Cardoso, Alejandro Kunold
abstract: We develop a Lie-Jordan geometric formulation of finite-dimensional open quantum dynamics, building on the algebraic framework introduced in our previous work (arXiv:2606.26477). The Hilbert-Schmidt operator space is endowed with an orthonormal Hermitian basis, in which the commutator and anticommutator are encoded by the structure tensors \(C_{μν}{}^λ\) and \(B_{μν}{}^λ\). Within this formulation, the von Neumann and Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan equations admit a direct component representation. Our central result is the identification of a basis-independent universal trilinear dissipative map, \( \mathcal D(X,Y)Z=XZY-\frac12\{YX,Z\}, \) whose components define a universal operator-space tensor depending only on the Lie-Jordan structure tensors. The physical dissipator is obtained by contracting this tensor with the expansion coefficients of the Lindblad operators and the Kossakowski matrix, thereby separating the universal algebraic structure from the model-dependent physical information. We further show that the combinations \((B+C)\) and \((B-C)\) generate internal left and right transports, allowing the elementary dissipative map to be expressed as a left-right bimodule action corrected by an ordered Jordan contribution. The universal map satisfies basis-independent trace and Hermitian-conjugation identities, from which trace preservation, Hermiticity preservation of the complete dissipator, and the reality of its component representation in a Hermitian Hilbert-Schmidt basis follow. We also derive its Hilbert-Schmidt adjoint and illustrate the formalism for a qubit with pure dephasing and amplitude-damping channels. This construction provides a tensorial and affine-geometric interpretation of the universal superoperator structure derived in arXiv:2606.26477 while keeping the algebraic and model-dependent sectors explicitly separated.
summary: This work introduces a Lie-Jordan geometric framework to provide a universal algebraic interpretation of dissipative evolution in open quantum systems. By decomposing the GKLS master equation into universal structural tensors and model-specific terms, it cleanly separates the underlying mathematical structure from the physics. This offers a powerful, systematic tool for analyzing any system undergoing Markovian dissipation.
main_problem: The paper develops a Lie-Jordan geometric formulation to systematically analyze the algebraic structure underlying open quantum dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation.
main_result: It successfully separates the universal, basis-independent algebraic structure of dissipation from the model-dependent physical parameters (Lindblad operators and Kossakowski matrix).
method: The authors endow the Hilbert-Schmidt operator space with an orthonormal basis and encode quantum commutators/anticommutators using Lie and Jordan structure tensors to derive a universal trilinear dissipative map.
model_or_system: The focus is on finite-dimensional open quantum systems whose evolution is described by the Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation. The formalism is tested using qubit examples exhibiting pure dephasing and amplitude damping.
key_observables: The component representation of the dissipator, $\dot{ho}_\lambda$, and the resulting Bloch vector dynamics ($\dot{\mathbf{r}}$).
important_parameters: Lindblad operators ($L_\alpha$), Kossakowski matrix ($\gamma_{\alpha eta}$), and the Lie/Jordan structure tensors ($C$ and $B$).
main_assumptions: The system evolution is assumed to be Markovian, completely positive, and trace-preserving.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the focus is on algebraic derivations and component equations rather than visual figure summaries.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general geometric framework using structure tensors for commutators/anticommutators to deriving a universal dissipative map. It then applies this formalism to verify known results (like trace preservation) and illustrates it with specific qubit channels, concluding by showing equivalence to standard ordered-product derivations.
why_interesting: This provides a deep algebraic and geometric underpinning for open quantum dynamics, offering tools to analyze the structure of dissipation independent of the specific physical Hamiltonian or Lindblad operators used.
